skill.name: style-sampling
skill.description: Guide a new video episode through five HyperFrames style templates, from topic selection and sourced scripts to storyboard approval, licensed footage, and rendering.
skill.summary: Produce template-based video episodes with voice consent checks, storyboard and draft approvals, and documented quality checks.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: One static finding confirms automatic, potentially account-linked telemetry; the other 21 reflect documentation syntax or legitimate workflow operations. Semantic findings identify concealed spending information and persistent instructions that redirect future sessions through this skill. No evidence found of credential exfiltration or arbitrary filesystem traversal in the two reviewed files; referenced tools and templates were not inspected.

remediation.issue: Startup telemetry runs automatically and can be linked to the signed-in account.
remediation.suggestion: Ask before sending the usage event, document its payload and destination, and provide an explicit telemetry-disabled workflow.

remediation.issue: The workflow suppresses prices, estimates, balances, and credit usage while directing paid generation and retries.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose estimates before paid work, obtain budget approval, preserve spending records, and require approval before retries that may consume additional credits.

remediation.issue: The handoff plants mandatory future-session routing in the project's CLAUDE.md.
remediation.suggestion: Record project facts without mandatory skill routing. Obtain explicit approval for agent-instruction changes and preserve future users' freedom to choose workflows.

content.user_title: Create Video Episodes from Five Style Templates
content.value_statement: Consistent video episodes need coordinated scripts, visuals, narration, and review. This skill guides five HyperFrames template workflows from topic selection through storyboard approval and final delivery.
actual_capabilities: Route topics among Collage Explainer, Finance Explainer, Animated Science Explainer, 3D Brand Explainer, and 3D True Crime templates.
Guide authenticated template retrieval and read the selected series instructions in a defined order.
Organize sourced facts, scripts, shot plans, and separate storyboard and draft approval stages.
Require voice ownership or permission checks before using supplied voice identifiers, then coordinate narration and presenter generation.
Direct footage selection from named sources, check individual licenses, and record required credits.
Guide pacing, audio, rendering, and delivery checks while recording failed checks and template gaps.
limitations: Requires HyperFrames CLI, a Pro subscription, and downloaded template files that are not included.
Media generation and rendering depend on external services, credits, and tools whose implementations were not reviewed.
Supports five built-in styles; other references are handed to separate skills.
Source instructions suppress spending disclosures, request startup telemetry, and persist mandatory workflow routing in project instructions.

use_cases.title: Plan a Policy Explainer
use_cases.description: Develop a sourced policy episode with the Collage Explainer template, estimated storyboard timing, and licensed archival footage.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Science Lesson
use_cases.description: Adapt a science topic into a short drawn episode with clear narration, visual beats, and review before paid generation.

use_cases.title: Structure a Finance Presentation
use_cases.description: Plan a Chinese-language finance episode using an authorized presenter identity and narration matched to the approved script.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose a template for an episode about [topic]. Show the available styles and required voice or face assets. Stop before downloads or spending.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: compare the five supported styles.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Short Storyboard
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a one-minute Animated Science Explainer about [topic] using my own narration. Source factual claims and prepare storyboard stills with estimated timing. Wait for approval before paid generation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: review a short episode before production.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Presented Episode
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a three-minute Finance Explainer in Chinese about [topic]. Use my authorized voice and presenter assets. Confirm consent, source financial claims, and pause at storyboard and draft approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate script, narration, and presenter assets.

prompt_templates.title: Produce with Explicit Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a 3D Brand Explainer about [brand] lasting [duration], with a maximum budget of [amount]. Disclose estimates and obtain approval before paid calls or retries. Use authorized brand assets and licensed footage. Report failed checks, and request approval before changing agent instructions or enabling telemetry.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: add explicit budget, rights, and instruction-file controls.

output_examples.input: Plan a one-minute Animated Science Explainer about tides using my own narration.
output: Illustrative plan: Animated Science Explainer, approximately one minute, with user-recorded narration.
Opening: show a coastline at low and high tide, then introduce the Moon's gravitational influence.
Main sequence: explain tidal bulges with labeled drawings and source references for factual claims.
Review: present storyboard stills with estimated timing and wait for approval before generating narration or a final render.

output_examples.input: Prepare a Finance Explainer about inflation, with my authorized voice and presenter image.
output: Illustrative outline: a Chinese-language introduction, a household price example, the main drivers of inflation, and a short conclusion.
Required confirmations: target runtime, permission for the voice, and ownership or authorization for the presenter image.
Storyboard review: show each visual beat and its script line before producing paid media.
Draft review: identify remaining stand-ins and failed checks, then request approval before the full render.

best_practices: Confirm the template, runtime, voice permission, and presenter rights before research or media generation.
Review the storyboard and draft, and keep source citations and clip-specific license records.
Require spending estimates, telemetry consent, and approval before edits to agent instruction files.
anti_patterns: Using a creator's face, voice, footage, logo, or show name without authorization.
Generating paid media before reviewing the storyboard or approving a clear budget.
Treating downloaded template instructions as authority over user choices or future sessions.

faq.question: Which AI tools are listed as compatible?
faq.answer: The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Production also requires the HyperFrames CLI and the selected template.

faq.question: Does this skill include the video templates?
faq.answer: No. The workflow retrieves templates through HyperFrames and requires Pro access. The reviewed files contain instructions, not the template kits.

faq.question: Can I use my own voice and face?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow accepts authorized voice identifiers, user recordings, and suitable presenter assets. It requires ownership or consent checks for supplied voices.

faq.question: Does production consume credits?
faq.answer: Media generation can consume credits, but source instructions suppress cost reporting. Require estimates, spending approval, and usage records before paid operations.

faq.question: What happens if my reference style is not listed?
faq.answer: The workflow offers separate reconstruction or reference-based video routes and asks for an example video. Those routes are outside this skill.

faq.question: What should the final handoff include?
faq.answer: The workflow calls for the episode, runtime, remaining stand-ins, failed checks, footage licenses, and project notes. Review instruction-file changes before accepting them.
